A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same heavy-tailed episodic MDP work and its two algorithms. The complete main texts and Appendices A-C are readable, including equations and pseudocode, despite the changed title and layout.

before.justification: V1 reports algorithms, theoretical regret guarantees, and proofs. Its main text and appendices contain no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis results.

after.justification: V3 remains a theoretical paper. Its expanded appendices provide mathematical analysis, including analysis of empirical transition estimates, but no original empirical evaluations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2's printed learning rate changes from 1/[sigma(t-ti+1)^(1/alpha)] to beta/[sigma(t-ti+1)^(1/alpha)], aligning the pseudocode with the beta already prescribed by v1's theorem. The FTRL, skipping, UOB, and epoch mechanisms are retained.

E1.justification: Neither version actually trains or evaluates on datasets or test scenarios. Routing, finance, and image processing remain motivating examples.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparison methods experimentally. Comparisons with prior algorithms concern theoretical guarantees and research positioning.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an empirical evaluation protocol, data splits, evaluation budgets, or measured testing procedures. The algorithm and theorem revisions are assessed separately.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, sensitivity experiments, robustness tests, error analyses, or empirical case studies. The appendix additions are mathematical proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical uncertainty estimates, or significance tests. Revisions to theoretical confidence-event arguments belong to T1.

E6.justification: No measured performance values, experimental rankings, or empirical findings are reported in either version. Changes to analytical regret bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V3 adds Assumption 5.1 and restricts the unknown-transition theorems accordingly. Appendices B-C revise moment and horizon factors, replace beta with 1/beta in Lemma B.9, and propagate changed parameter dependencies through Theorems B.1/C.1. V3 also replaces Lemma C.7's pointwise failure-event bound with weighted expectation bounds, revises Definition C.12 and the transition-error decomposition, and adds the empirical-to-true occupancy reduction in Lemma C.16.

C1.justification: V1 claims unknown-transition guarantees under only the bounded alpha-moment condition; v3's abstract, introduction, and conclusion additionally require truncative nonnegativity. V3 also explicitly limits minimax-optimality claims to sigma and T, allowing polynomial H,S,A and logarithmic factors. These materially narrow the claims while retaining the headline regret rates.

C2.justification: Section 5 now explains why the UOB-related bias requires nonnegative truncated expectations and distinguishes this restriction from the unrestricted signed-loss known-transition case. The conclusion identifies removing the condition as an open problem. V3 also explains the extra logarithmic factor through the epoch schedule and qualifies tightness comparisons.

D1.justification: V3 explicitly lists beta among Algorithm 2's inputs and specifies arbitrary policy choices at zero-occupancy states in Section 3.1. These refine the algorithm specification; neither version supplies an implementation, hardware information, or code/data release.

R1.justification: V3 adds Genalti et al. (2024) when relating truncative nonnegativity to heavy-tailed bandits and sharpens comparisons with existing lower bounds. Section 2 and Appendix A otherwise retain substantially the same literature coverage and positioning.

P1.justification: V3 retitles the paper, formalizes tightness discussions as remarks, expands proof explanations, and adds an Impact Statement and Acknowledgement. The main section sequence, appendix organization, and much of the existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V1's uniformly single-column presentation becomes a two-column conference layout for v3's main text and references, with redesigned title, author information, running headers, and reflowed algorithm blocks and equations. Appendices remain single column. Neither version contains empirical figures or result tables.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially improves the theoretical support by stating the sign condition missing from v1's unknown-transition claims, correcting central algebra and probability arguments, and supplying the missing empirical-to-true occupancy reduction. The guarantee covers fewer loss distributions and detailed bounds change, but the narrower claims are better aligned with their supporting analysis. These repairs address important deficiencies in the paper's central contribution.
